source_solutions.independent_solution: Let O be the sphere centre and R>0 its radius. Central reflection sends an arbitrary M to M'=2O-M, so M'-O=-(M-O) and |OM'|=|OM|=R. This involution sends the entire sphere onto itself, proving that O is its centre of symmetry. A half-turn about any line through O and a reflection in any plane through O fix O and preserve distances, so each is a symmetry. There are infinitely many such axes and infinitely many such planes. Conversely a symmetry must preserve the unique sphere centre, so its axis or plane must contain O.

source_solutions.independent_solution: For a plane P through the centre O, sphere intersection P is the set of planar points M with |OM|=R. It is a circle in P centred at O, of radius R (a great circle), not its filled disk.

Using S=(1,-2,0), squared distances are SA^2=0^2+0^2+3^2=9, SB^2=2^2+(-1)^2+1^2=6, SC^2=0^2+3^2+(sqrt(2))^2=11, SD^2=(-1)^2+(-1)^2+(sqrt(7))^2=9. Radius squared is 9; exactly A and D belong to the surface. B is inside and C outside.

source_solutions.independent_solution: R>0 follows the seed's sphere definition. On Ox set y=z=0, yielding x=+-R; on Oy set x=z=0, yielding y=+-R; on Oz set x=y=0, yielding z=+-R. All six distinct intersections are (R,0,0),(-R,0,0),(0,R,0),(0,-R,0),(0,0,R),(0,0,-R).

The entire line SO consists of t(3,4,5) for real t. Substitution gives (9+16+25)t^2=200, hence t^2=4 and t=+-2. Its two intersections are (6,8,10) and (-6,-8,-10). Restricting to a positive ray would wrongly discard the second intersection.

source_solutions.independent_solution: Because p>0, |OA|=sqrt(9+4+36)p=7p and radius=p. For every sphere point X the reverse triangle inequality gives |AX|>=||OA|-|OX||=6p. Equality is attained at X=A/7=(3p/7,-2p/7,6p/7), whose norm is p. Thus the point-to-sphere distance is 6p, not the centre distance 7p or farthest distance 8p.

source_solutions.independent_solution: The general equation is (x-a)^2+(y-b)^2+(z-c)^2=R^2. For S=(2,-1,3), R=4 it becomes (x-2)^2+(y+1)^2+(z-3)^2=16. For S=(-5,0,7), R=sqrt(3) it becomes (x+5)^2+y^2+(z-7)^2=3. Both cases need centre-coordinate subtraction and squared radius.
